guides.title: Three different evidence questions
guides.intro: A mechanism, an association and an individual conclusion are different kinds of evidence.
cards: Mechanism
How can a biological process work?
Enzymes, transporters, cells and model experiments.
Association
What varies together in a study?
A statistical result needs its sample, effect and uncertainty.
Individual conclusion
What does this mean for this person?
Clinical and genetic interpretation needs additional evidence.
guides.note: A connection between these questions needs evidence; it is not automatic.
guides.caption: Use the question to recognise the scope of a claim. A normal pathway does not prove a defect; an association does not prove an individual cause.
guides.alt: Three different evidence questions. A mechanism, an association and an individual conclusion are different kinds of evidence. A connection between these questions needs evidence; it is not automatic.

guides.title: Make a handover visible
guides.intro: A practical checklist for following a referral or transfer; ask the service which process applies.
cards: The sender
What was sent, when and to whom?
Keep the referral, summary and reference.
The receiver
Was it received and accepted?
Separate delivery, triage, acceptance and responsibility.
The next action
Who does what, by when?
Record the plan, contact and how an overdue action is escalated.
guides.note: A sent message is not the same event as an accepted handover or a completed action.
guides.caption: This is a record-organising tool, not a declaration that every referral guarantees treatment. Ask for the actual status and next decision.
guides.alt: Make a handover visible. A practical checklist for following a referral or transfer; ask the service which process applies. A sent message is not the same event as an accepted handover or a completed action.

guides.title: A short account with useful detail
guides.intro: Lead with what has changed and the decision you need; keep the supporting detail available.
cards: Change and impact
What is different from your baseline?
Name the practical effect and relevant dates.
Evidence and uncertainty
Which record supports which point?
Separate observation, your report and a working hypothesis.
Decision needed
What answer or next action are you asking for?
Ask who owns it and when you will receive the answer.
guides.note: A clear short account can link to a full chronology without trying to fit everything into one box.
guides.caption: A template for structuring an appointment question or written update. It does not replace reporting urgent concerns to the relevant clinical service.
guides.alt: A short account with useful detail. Lead with what has changed and the decision you need; keep the supporting detail available. A clear short account can link to a full chronology without trying to fit everything into one box.

guides.title: Browse, search and keep your place
guides.intro: Three routes through this website, with the current section always visible.
cards: Browse by topic
Open the menu, then choose a category.
Only the selected branch opens; the current page is marked.
Search a specific term
Use search when you know the word or phrase.
Results include the section path as well as the title.
Move through parents
Use the location path or optional desktop sidebar.
Return to a parent section without retracing every link.
guides.note: The location path describes the topic hierarchy, not your private browsing history.
guides.caption: The menu and breadcrumb work together. On larger screens you can pin the explorer; on a phone it opens as a drawer.
guides.alt: Browse, search and keep your place. Three routes through this website, with the current section always visible. The location path describes the topic hierarchy, not your private browsing history.
